text:
Ashley: Heads up — EU-west GPUs are saturated right now, queue depth spiking for p50/p95. Seeing a lot of small interactive queries from freemium customers.
Mike: ack. Is this the nightly training traffic or normal user traffic?
Ashley: normal inference traffic — sudden surge from a partner demo. Not training.
Priya: Can we soft-route low-priority tenants to other regions instead of dropping? Egress costs will increase but better than errors.
Juan: We have two levers: admission control per-tenant + cross-region negotiation handshake. We could attempt a short-lived crosszone handoff if latency budget allows.
Rini: Agree. Proposal: implement a capacity negotiation RPC that returns a bite-sized token with a ttl that other regions can honor. If token accepted, route request to remote region with attached "remote-accepted" header.
Ashley: That sounds good. Need to ensure model fallback too — we can replace gptx-large-8k -> gptx-medium-4k when moving cross-region to reduce GPU memory and infer cost.
Mike: Also need to enforce per-tenant soft-SLA. If tenant has "max_remote_pct": 20 we shouldn't spill >20% of their requests.
Priya: Also suggest a budgeted egress cap per account for the month so we can avoid surprises. Put flag in tenant profile like "egress_spill_threshold".
Juan: Sketch of negotiation flow:
```json
POST /v1/routing/negotiate
{
  "origin_region":"eu-west",
  "required_slots":1,
  "max_latency_ms":200,
  "tenant_id":"acct_123",
  "cost_priority":"minimize_local_cost"
}
```
Response: token + accept|reject + suggested_model_variant + estimated_cost. Token TTL 3s.
Ashley: Implementation question: do we prefer trying closest secondary region (eu-north) first or fall back to NA if all EU is full? Closest first reduces latency/egress.
Rini: Closest-first with a scoring function: score = latency_penalty * latency_ms + egress_cost_weight * estimated_egress_bytes + model_cost_weight * model_vram. Tunable per-org.
Mike: We need admission-control counters in the local region that decrement when we hand off token. Race conditions: if token accepted but by the time request arrives the remote region is at capacity. TTL helps but we should have a quick reject path and optional retry to next region.
Priya: For tenants on Dedicated, honor isolation: never route outside the tenant's region unless explicit opt-in. Add a flag in tenant config: "allow_cross_region": true/false.
Juan: Monitoring: emit metrics "routing.handshake.attempt", "routing.handshake.accept", "routing.handoff.latency", and per-tenant "remote_spill_pct". Alert on remote_spill_pct > configured threshold.
Ashley: For rollout — canary in eu-north at 5% of traffic, ramp to 25% after 30m if error rate <1% and p95 latency within 1.5x baseline.
Mike: On cost: ops asked to estimate egress delta. Priya can you run a quick model with current 1h traffic?
Priya: On it. Initial estimate: if 15% of EU traffic routes to NA it adds ~$900/day egress for that partner.
Rini: Could do an economic knob: prefer local model downgrade (cheaper) over cross-region if tenant cost_sensitivity high.
Ashley: Let's capture config changes:
```yaml
routing_defaults:
  max_remote_pct: 0.15
  remote_ttl_s: 3
  prefer_local_downgrade: true
  scoring_weights:
    latency_penalty: 1.0
    egress_cost_weight: 2.0
    model_cost_weight: 0.5
```
Juan: I'll draft the RPC and scoring lib today. Rini can help with token semantics + TTL enforcement. Mike can add admission counters + race handling. Priya to report egress numbers and recommend thresholds for the partner.
Ashley: Also add a runtime flag to disable cross-region globally in case of network blackhole between regions. @deploy-bot can you provision a feature-flag?
deploy-bot: Feature flag "routing.cross_region_handoff" created in staging.
Mike: I'll implement the counters and a short circuit (fast-fail) if token age > TTL on arrival.
Priya: Egress estimates done — sharing in thread: 900/day peak, 2700/week. Will add spreadsheet link after.
Ashley: Thanks team — let's sync in 30m for final handoff before canary. :thumbsup:
